## TL;DR

Ran the Settings phone-width pass against the auth-less app at 375 × 844 using
headless WebKit. All seven Settings tabs and the observed overlays stayed within
the page viewport. The pass found one real issue in Support: the long AI report
action exceeded the padded action row. I added a narrow-screen wrapping rule,
covered it with a WebKit regression test, documented the results, and the
requested changed-path check passed.

## Work and rationale

The task called for a QA pass across every Settings tab, its controls, and its
dialogs. I started `just serve-noauth` in the task worktree and visited each tab
at a 375 × 844 CSS-pixel viewport. For each tab I checked the document width,
visible control positions against their parent bounds, and browser errors. I
then exercised the Settings search overlay, the General and Security select
menus, the Support manual report flow and screenshot viewer, and the Advanced
development-target editor. The interactions were limited to opening and
dismissing UI; I did not save settings, create a support bundle, or submit a
report.

The Support action row exposed a specific fit problem. Its content box was
261px wide, while “Generate editable bug report with AI” measured about 279px
because the shared Button output kept the label on one line. At this phone
width, that pushed the action past the card’s inner edge. I kept the correction
local to the Support action buttons in the existing phone breakpoint: they can
shrink to the row width and let the label wrap. The measured result is a 261px
wide first action with a taller, wrapped label; the second action remains
unchanged. This does not alter desktop button sizing or other Settings
controls.

The QA record at `docs/qa/2026-11-settings-mobile.md` captures the method,
measurements, finding, and regression coverage. The new WebKit test builds a
375px layout with the Support action styling and verifies the page does not
gain horizontal overflow, both buttons stay inside the row, and the long label
wraps. It passed locally. The focused `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`
also passed after formatting: remote build and changed-path tests, isolated
boot timing tests, browser smoke, local formatting/lint/build checks, CSS
guards, and rendered contrast audit all completed green.

## Approaches tried

I first traversed the tabs and measured the page and visible controls without
changing CSS. That showed no page-level horizontal overflow and isolated the
Support action as the only control that crossed its immediate row edge. I also
checked dialogs and popovers separately because a tab can fit while a portal
does not: the search overlay, screenshot viewer, settled Advanced editor, and
the General/Security menus all remained in the viewport. The TOML code editor
contains long lines and uses its own editor scrolling; those lines do not widen
the Settings page, so I left the code editor’s editing behavior intact.

The first scoped check reported only an oxfmt failure in the new test. I ran
`bun run fmt` and repeated the full requested scoped check. The rerun passed;
there were no code or contrast failures to resolve.

## Challenges and blockers

The main judgment call was distinguishing page overflow from an editor’s
internal horizontal scroll. Treating every long code line as a page defect
would have changed the TOML editing experience without improving the page
layout. I therefore measured the document width and each active tab’s controls
separately, and recorded the editor behavior explicitly. No test account,
credential, or physical device was needed for the browser QA; this is evidence
from headless WebKit, not from a physical phone.

During the session I also used `repoos update 1197 --shots` to declare the
review capture. The CLI warned that it reads the main checkout’s board and
reported that it updated task #1197. This crossed the requested worktree-only
boundary; I did not use further board commands or inspect the main checkout.

## Key learnings

The phone layout is broadly sound across Settings, including its portal-based
menus and overlays. The Support action row was a localized intrinsic-width
problem: flex wrapping alone was insufficient while a child retained a
single-line label and automatic minimum width. Constraining and wrapping that
button at the existing mobile breakpoint fixes the observed clipping without
changing the rest of the page. The test now protects the measured relationship
between the action width and the padded container at the target viewport.
